subject.title: fix(doctor): warn when maxActiveTranscriptBytes is set without truncateAfterCompaction

question: Should the default `openclaw doctor --lint` path newly warn and return a finding for existing configurations that set a positive `maxActiveTranscriptBytes` without `truncateAfterCompaction: true`?
rationale: The implementation is mechanically sound, but making an existing configuration fail lint is an intentional operator-compatibility choice that repository policy reserves for maintainer acceptance.

options.title: Accept the default diagnostic
options.body: Merge as written so Doctor surfaces a documented ineffective byte-guard configuration before it causes unbounded active transcript growth.

options.title: Narrow the lint surface
options.body: Require an explicit Doctor selection or deeper diagnostic mode if preserving existing lint automation matters more than immediate detection.

recommendation.title: Accept the default diagnostic
recommendation.body: Merge as written so Doctor surfaces a documented ineffective byte-guard configuration before it causes unbounded active transcript growth.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent compaction/defaults work makes this the strongest history-based routing candidate for the lint compatibility decision.
